model.summary_ko:
r3(수정 2회차): 검증자 지적 22건(물리 8, 기하 14)을 모두 다시 계산해 보고 고쳤다. 기각한 것은 없고, 3건은 부분 수용이다: 흑 노치 들림, DW 가장자리 값, 레버 봉 마개 길이.

가장 큰 변경은 업스톱 레일 고정이다. 서로 겹치던 M5 와셔 Ø20과 너트 9조를 없앴다. 대신 핀 칸마다 탭 강철 띠(SS400 4T×20)를 하나씩 밑에서 주머니에 밀어 넣고(천장 3.5), 손나사 8개를 체결한다. 손나사 위치는 레일 FE 탐색으로 x8/23/55.4/70.4/97/112/141.6/156.5, y182에 정했다. 지렛대 계수는 2.18에서 1.86으로, 1 N당 최대 나사 장력은 1.74에서 1.54로 내려갔다. 접시 스프링은 3 병렬 × 3 직렬(이동 0.45 mm)로 바꾸고, 출력 드라이버 Ø30(테두리 20 N)으로 조이며, 24 h 뒤와 운반 뒤 다시 평평하게 조인다. 상시 지압은 띠를 탄성층 위의 유한 보로 풀어 1.90 MPa다(검증자 9.6~14 MPa). 핀을 y152까지 앞으로 늘려(앞 연장은 0.2 얇게) 편심을 넣은 이음 응력이 한 건반 2.0 m/s에서 3.20 MPa, 뒷벽까지 넣은 모델로 4.80 MPa다. 한 건반 2.5 m/s 나사 장력은 360 N으로 예하중 422 N 아래이고, 끝 부속(볼 위 손나사 추가)은 385 N이다. 5~20 ms에 걸쳐 치는 굴린 화음에서는 이음이 닫힌 채다.

유령 재타건: 0.6·0.7·0.8 N 누름을 더했다. 패드 실효 e를 0.06(합격선 0.07)으로 낮추고, 재무장선을 50 %로 올리고, 펌웨어 거름 규칙을 넣었다. 설계값에서 최대 42 %이고, 합격선에서 넘는 경우는 거름 규칙이 잡는다.

흑 노치: 스냅 노치(입술 z20.75, 계단 블록)를 넣고 봉은 블록 사이 받침에 놓았다. 설계값에서 들림은 최대 0.152 mm다. 재료가 나쁘면 r2의 절반쯤인 0.28~0.59 mm로 남으므로 단계 0 합격선을 둔다(흑 패드 K ≥ 25, 앞 펠트 e ≤ 0.22). 그 밖의 변경:
- 강철 앞 윗모서리 2.0×45° 모따기: 캡 밑 출력 벽 0.80 mm
- 탭 옆 놀음 ±0.05와 커버 위치 핀 놀음 ±0.1을 스윕에 넣음(헤드 22.04, 흑 밑폭 10.4): 1.3 mm 미만 0쌍
- 백 패드 틈을 +0.20으로 바꿔 캡스턴 충격을 16.7 N으로 억제
- 백 DW 52 g으로 립 y0 47.1 g
- L 서비스 블록, 두 봉 161.4 ± 0.2, 밸런스 핀·홈 치수, 치수표와 geometry.json 수정

model_v4.py·run_all.py로 다시 돌려 geometry.json, metrics.json, results.txt, DESIGN.md를 새로 만들었다. 판정식 17개가 모두 통과했다.

대가: 커버 윗면 z78.0(r2 75.3), 손나사 머리 z80.7(r2 76.2), 모듈 2.03 kg, 비용 +130,400원(기본 713,619원), 필라멘트 6.54 kg · 436 h.

resolved.item: PH1 (major) 가벼운 누름(0.6~0.8 N)에서 유령 재타건
resolved.resolution: 수용. 0.6/0.7/0.8 N 누름을 2.0·2.5 m/s 판정에 넣음. 패드 실효 e 0.10 → 설계 0.06, 단계 0 합격선 0.07, 재무장선 40 → 50 %, 펌웨어 거름 규칙(120 ms 안, 오름 < 60 %, 내려오는 속도 < 0.3 m/s) 추가. 설계값에서 자석 최대 42 %(< 50 %). 합격선 0.07에서는 53 %지만 넘는 경우(흑 2.5 m/s, 0.6 N)는 내려오는 속도가 0.15 m/s라 거름 규칙이 잡음. 연타(t50) 14.2 / 14.8 Hz, 마찰 2배 13.7 / 13.8 Hz. 검증자 제안 e 0.05 대신 0.06/0.07로 둔 까닭: e가 낮을수록 업스톱 힘이 커짐(2.0 m/s 185 N, r2 152 N).

resolved.item: PH2 (major) 흑 노치 들림·키퍼 무접촉이 재료 가정값에만 의존
resolved.resolution: 부분 수용. 스냅 노치 적용: 블록 밑면이 봉 중심 아래 0.75, 감싸는 각 223°, 입술 구역만 내려가는 계단 블록, 봉은 블록 사이 받침 11개, 빠짐 4~8 N. 설계값 들림 최대 0.152 mm. 흑 2.0 m/s 들림: 패드 K 10.6일 때 0.28 mm(검증자 r2 0.63), 앞 펠트 e 0.35일 때 0.43 mm(검증자 r2 0.97). 건반은 봉에서 빠지지 않음. 4~8 N으로 빠지는 스냅은 위쪽으로 무르므로 단계 0 합격선(흑 패드 K ≥ 25, 앞 펠트 e ≤ 0.22, 패드 e ≤ 0.07)을 둠. 합격선 재료에서 2.0 m/s까지 0.148 mm, 2.5 m/s 스타카토 0.213 mm. 뒤 누름 펠트 안은 블록이 건반 윗판 속에 있어 불가.

resolved.item: PH3 (major) 너트 트랩 지붕 지압 9.6~14 MPa
resolved.resolution: 수용. 와셔와 너트를 없애고 핀 칸마다 탭 강철 띠 SS400 4T×20(지붕 3.5). 띠를 탄성층 위의 유한 보로 풀어 최대 지압 1.90 MPa(나사 구멍 ↔ 띠 끝 5.9 이상), 레일 받침 0.57 MPa.

resolved.item: PH4 (major) 예하중이 앉음에 약하고 끝 부속 하중 미보고
resolved.resolution: 수용. 접시 스프링 3×3(이동 0.45 mm): 앉음 30 / 50 / 80 µm에서 428 / 408 / 377 N 남음(검증자 r2 378 / 323 / 251). 24 h 뒤와 운반 뒤 다시 조임. 나사 y182, FE 탐색으로 1 N당 최대 1.54(r2 1.74). 한 건반 2.5 m/s 나사 360 N < 422 N. 끝 부속은 볼 위 손나사 추가: 한 건반 2.5 m/s 최대 385 N, A0~B0 한꺼번에 2.0 m/s 392 N(닫힘; 검증자 r2 559 N 열림). 2.5 m/s 동시는 497 N으로 열림(드문 경우). 결과표에 보고.

resolved.item: PH5 (major) 핀 이음 편심 굽힘 누락
resolved.resolution: 수용. σ = N/A + N·e·c/I로 계산. 핀을 y152까지 앞으로 늘림. 한 건반 2.0 m/s: 핀만 3.20 MPa, 뒷벽 포함 4.80 MPa(< 5; 검증자 r2 9.05). 6건반 한꺼번에 2.0 m/s는 10.1 MPa(드문 경우). 5 / 10 / 20 ms에 걸쳐 굴린 화음은 2.6 / 3.2 / 3.2 MPa, 이음 닫힘.

resolved.item: PH6 (major) R3 캡이 톱날 강철 모서리 위 0.03 mm
resolved.resolution: 수용. 강철 앞 윗모서리 2.0×45° 줄 모따기. 모델에 캡-강철 최소 벽 검사를 넣어 0.80 mm(모따기 없으면 0.030). 검증자 제안 1.5×45°는 모따기 아래 꼭짓점에서 벽 0.74.

resolved.item: PH7 (minor) 구름 확인 없음
resolved.resolution: 수용. 쉼과 2.0 m/s 누른 채 기록으로 구름 비를 계산. 봉이 풀리는 순간은 가이드 탭이 짝힘으로 받으며 최대 0.02 N. 탭 옆 놀음 ±0.05 = (8.6 − 7.5 − 2 × 0.5) / 2.

resolved.item: PH8 (minor) DW 가장자리 값, 프리즘이 질량 모델과 다름
resolved.resolution: 부분 수용. 백 DW 목표 52.0 g으로 립 y0 47.1 g. 마찰 2배 DW 55.9 / 55.8 g과 흑 바닥 UW 17.4 g은 민감도 값으로 인정(단계 0에서 퍼티·보조 스프링). 리브·자석 보스 리브·블록 웹·블록 윗면을 geometry.json에 내보냄.

resolved.item: G1 (critical) 와셔 Ø20 겹침으로 만들 수 없음
resolved.resolution: 수용. 핀 칸마다 탭 띠 1개, 나사 8개(칸마다 2개). 띠 ↔ 핀 0.30, 나사 구멍 ↔ 띠 끝 5.9 이상, 이웃 모듈 띠 사이 4.2, 머리 사이 2.9 이상. 고정-고정 검사와 geometry.json에 띠 추가.

resolved.item: G2 (major) 이음이 닫힌 동안 지붕 굽힘 누락, 주머니가 핀을 자름
resolved.resolution: 수용. 닫힌 동안 지붕은 레일과 띠 사이에 예하중으로 끼워져 가장자리 전단만 받음(2.0 m/s 1.67 MPa, 2.5 m/s 2.12 MPa). 열린 경우 굽힘(층 안, 한꺼번에 친 화음 22.3 MPa)도 보고. 핀 평면 나사를 없애 주머니가 칸 안에 있음(나사 ↔ 핀 중심 7.0 이상).

resolved.item: G3 (major) 커버 놀음이 스윕에 없음
resolved.resolution: 수용. Ø3 위치 핀 2개로 레일과 커버를 ±0.10으로 잡고 자석 2개를 둠. 스윕에서 가림판을 부풀려 레버 ↔ 가림판 1.74, 건반 ↔ 가림판 1.31(검증자 r2 0.93 / 0.90).

resolved.item: G4 (major) 가이드 탭 옆 놀음이 요 모델에 없음
resolved.resolution: 수용. ±0.05를 모든 건반 프리즘에 더함. 헤드 틈 1.46(헤드 22.04), 꼬리 틈 1.62, 흑 밑폭 10.4. 건반-건반 1.30, 흑-백 1.33.

resolved.item: G5 (major) 접시 스프링을 손으로 평평하게 조이는 것은 믿을 수 없음
resolved.resolution: 수용. 조임 0.30 N·m를 출력 드라이버 Ø30(테두리 20 N)으로. 스택 이동 0.45 mm(약 0.9바퀴)라 멈춤이 뚜렷함. 단계 0에서 로드셀로 422 N 이상 확인.

resolved.item: G6 (minor) 서비스 블록
resolved.resolution: 수용. L 블록(발 y195.8~205 × 3 두께, 기둥 y196~198.6, 폭 9), 윗면 z31.80으로 레버가 쉼보다 0.48° 낮게 머묾. 조립 때 모듈당 12개, 보관함에 3개.

resolved.item: G7 (minor) 밸런스 핀·홈 치수
resolved.resolution: 수용. 핀 ISO 2338 Ø2×12, 꼭대기 z23.30 ± 0.1(출력 높이 게이지), 구멍 바닥 z11.30. 홈은 출력 폭 3.2(천 포함 2.2), 깊이 2.5. 레일 앞 y133.5(핀 구멍 앞벽 2.0). 빼기에서 블록이 핀 위로 3.31 mm.

resolved.item: G8 (minor) 캐리어 출력·조립
resolved.resolution: 수용. 강철 칸 지지대, 강철은 밑에서 끼움, 모따기, 흑건 납은 접착 + 출력 뚜껑.

resolved.item: G9 (minor) 크로스바-탭 최소 0.58, 앞 펠트 모서리
resolved.resolution: 수용. 0.58(공차 뒤 0.28)로 보고, 탭 앞면에 천 0.5T. 앞 펠트를 y1.5~9.8로 잘라 크로스바·리브와 0.87 mm.

resolved.item: G10 (minor) 외곽 높이·운반
resolved.resolution: 수용. 맨 위 = 손나사 머리 z80.7(커버 z78.0)로 보고. 커버는 위치 핀 + 자석으로 고정. R18: 모듈 2.03 kg씩 하나씩 옮김.

resolved.item: G11 (minor) 치수표·내보내기 불일치
resolved.resolution: 수용. S05를 받침 홈에서 계산, 블록 실제 윗면과 계단, 보스 리브, 서비스 자세 14.5°(빼기에서 잡는 각), 끝 부속 복귀 넘침·서비스 자세, 1 N 정착 바닥을 dip으로 쓰고 강체 바닥은 dip_rigid로 분리, 주석 정리, 흑건 4종.

resolved.item: G12 (minor) 봉 길이 여유 0, 끝 벽 0.4
resolved.resolution: 부분 수용. 두 봉 모두 161.4 ± 0.2, 막힌 벽 1.2. 마개는 1.2(마개 ≥ 2면 끝 부싱 걸림이 0.85 mm뿐이라). 경화 봉은 길이로 잘라 주문.

resolved.item: G13 (minor) 레버 봉 꿰기
resolved.resolution: 수용. 간격 링을 봉에 나중에 끼우는 C-링으로, 꿰는 동안 레버는 L 서비스 블록 위.

resolved.item: G14 (minor) 스프링 자리
resolved.resolution: 수용. 포켓 Ø4.4×1.5에 접착, 컵 Ø6.4.

open_issues: 흑 노치 들림 0.2 mm 목표는 설계 재료값에서만 지켜진다. 패드 K 10.6이면 0.28 mm, 앞 펠트 e 0.35이면 2.5 m/s에서 0.59 mm로 남으므로 단계 0 합격선(흑 패드 K ≥ 25, 앞 펠트 e ≤ 0.22)에 달려 있다. 합격선 재료에서도 2.5 m/s 스타카토는 0.213 mm다.
업스톱 패드 실효 e 0.06(합격선 0.07)은 가정값이다. e 0.10이면 2.5 m/s·0.6~0.7 N 누름의 유령을 거름 규칙으로도 잡지 못한다. 단계 0 시험 1이 가장 먼저다.
스냅 노치의 빠짐 힘(4~8 N)과 입술 천 두께는 시험 전이다. 모델의 최대 당김은 2.72 N(설계값)이고, 나쁜 재료에서는 3.9 N까지 간다.
6건반을 0.1 ms 안에 한꺼번에 치면 레일 이음이 순간 열린다: 나사 613 / 779 N, 핀 이음 10.1 / 12.9 MPa(뒷벽 포함 14.5 / 18.5), 열린 동안 지붕 굽힘 22.3 / 28.3 MPa(층 안). 5 ms 이상 굴리면 닫힌다.
마찰 2배 연타가 13.7 / 13.8 Hz로 13.3 Hz 선에 가깝다. 모자라면 보조 스프링을 끼운다.
높이가 올랐다: 커버 z78.0, 손나사 머리 z80.7(r2 75.3 / 76.2). 20 mm 폭 띠 주머니 때문이다.
건반 빼기: 레버를 14.5°에 잡아야 하는데 브리지에 닿는 각 15.2°와 가깝고, 뽑기 틈은 0.52 mm, 당기는 힘은 6.9~9.8 N이다.
숨은 빔 11.9 MPa와 흑 꼬리 8.3 MPa의 반복 응력은 피로 자료가 없다. 단계 0 피로 시편으로 확인한다.

vs.lens: Physics and dynamics (round 1, adversarial). I wrote my own code and did not import model_v4.py: vsim.py is a 4-DOF free-notch key plus a 1-DOF lever, with Hunt-Crossley/Flores felts, Coulomb friction at the notch, notch lips, capstan, lever rod and guide, the tab y-stop and the keeper. I also wrote a quasi-static virtual-work statics routine, a rail model with bending and torsion (loads.py, rail_torsion.py), and a mass-property cross-check taken from the exported prisms (massprops.py). With the designer's inputs the statics match exactly and the nominal dynamics match within 1–9 %. The errors are in what was not tested: an fff that is too soft, the restitution calibration, the preload on the rail joint, the load path from the boss head into the fin, and friction at the notch lips.

errors.issue: The ghost re-trigger and notch-lift checks pass only under a soft fff and a light-rebound felt. The model's 'fff' is a constant 6 N push from rest, which reaches only 1.21 m/s (white) and 1.33 m/s (black) at the felt. The 80 g lever bounces off a wool up-stop and drives the key back up against the held finger. (1) With the designer's own fff and a 1.0 N hold, the white key front rises 5.1–6.5 mm and the magnet reaches 45–59 % of its travel, past the 40 % re-trigger line. The rise crosses 40 % at 22–27 ms and lands on the front felt again at 68–76 ms. That second note-on looks the same as a legitimate 14 Hz repeat, so firmware cannot filter it without dropping below 13.3 Hz. (2) With the brief's 2 N hold, the magnet crosses 40 % at a bottom speed of about 1.8–1.9 m/s (white: 43 %; at 2.3 m/s, 53–71 %). The key-front rise exceeds 2 mm from about 1.3 m/s. (3) Black notch lift is 0.25–0.27 mm at 1.66 m/s, 0.35–0.37 at 1.95 m/s and 0.49–0.53 at 2.47 m/s, above the 0.2 mm target. The cause is geometric: the black front stop at y55–59 lies ahead of the key's centre of percussion, so a rebound from the front felt lifts the notch whenever the lever has left the capstan. (4) The white up-stop felt reaches penetration 2.01–2.09 of its 2.0 mm at about 2.8 m/s (cap on the steel rail).
errors.fix: (a) Replace the plain 2T wool up-stop with a low-rebound pad (effective e ≤ 0.15, e.g. 1T felt face over 2 mm low-rebound PU or sorbothane) and make e ≤ 0.15 a stage-0 pass criterion. In my model this gives, after a 2 m/s strike with a 1 N hold: rise ≤ 1.78 mm, magnet ≤ 10 %. After the designer's fff with a 2 N hold: 0.50 mm. t40 is unchanged (33.5/27.7 ms). (b) Put about 2 g of tungsten putty at the black key front (y57) and move the black capstan from 180.54 to 181.13 to keep DW 51.0. Black notch lift at 1.95 m/s then falls from 0.22 to 0.13 mm; m_eff rises to 63 g. (c) Define fff by speed (≥ 2.0 m/s at the finger point, key and lever co-moving) and add a 1 N hold case to the ghost check. (d) Re-run the rail and screw loads with the new up-stop peaks: 77–171 N per key with a low-rebound pad, against 57.5 N now.
errors.evidence: run_dyn6.py, run_ghost_timing.py, run_fix.py, run_dyn8.py, run_blackfix.py (raw_outputs.txt). The comment in model_v4.py ("the effective restitution equals e (checked by felt_effective_e())") is false. errors.issue: The thumb-screw preload is unrealistic, which invalidates two conclusions. (1) Rest stress: the 1.36 MPa maximum constant stress uses a 40 N preload under the Ø7 end washer. The designer's own finger-tight torque of 0.05 N·m already gives 56–83 N (nut factor 0.3–0.2), which is 1.9–2.8 MPa. A normal finger-tight 0.1–0.2 N·m on a knurled head gives 111–333 N: 3.8–11.3 MPa bearing and 3.2–9.5 MPa punching shear on the PETG roof under the Ø7 washer, and 1.1–3.2 MPa bearing under the Ø12 washers. That breaks the < 2 MPa creep target, and creep then relaxes the preload. (2) Joint opening: with the rail pivoting on the boss rear edge at y200, the prying factor is (200 − 157.4)/16 = 2.66. With 40 N preload, my bending-plus-torsion rail model opens the rail-to-boss joint at a single-key up-stop force of 15.0 N (C and C#, on the 27.9 mm left overhang that has no screw) and 16.6–29.8 N for the other keys. The model's own mf peak is 20.9 N and ff is 36.2 N, so the steel rail lifts and re-seats on PETG at almost every mf+ note: a tick noise, a soft up-stop, and the preload cycling to zero, which self-loosens the unlocked thumb screws. Keeping the joint closed at 57.5 N fff needs at least 153 N of preload, which again exceeds 2 MPa in PETG.
errors.fix: Take PETG out of the preload path. Clamp the rail steel-to-steel onto M3 steel standoffs (or a steel bracket) anchored in the fins or frame, so the preload (≥ 200 N, set by a stop, not by feel) never loads the roof. Add a screw or boss at the left B|C fin, or shorten the 27.9 mm overhang. Lock the thumb screws (wave or spring washer under the head, or a thin nylon-insert nut). Re-state the maximum constant stress for the real preload.
errors.evidence: loads.py: preload versus torque table. rail_torsion.py: with 40 N preload the per-key opening forces are C 15.0, C# 15.0, D 18.4, E 18.4, F 17.5, G 23.8, A 19.1, B 16.6 N. model_v4.rest_stresses uses Fp = 40 N over the Ø7 washer.

errors.issue: The chord load path into PETG is under-estimated. The designer's '12.9 MPa fin tension' spreads the 612–615 N screw pull over 1.6 × 29.9 mm of fin. But the boss head (y180–200) sits on a 1.6 mm fin, so the junction is at most 1.6 × 20 = 32 mm²: 19.1 MPa of tension across the layers (the frame prints upright) under the designer's own 6-key chord. That is 48 % higher than reported and near PETG's layer strength. The worst chord (D–G) puts its 229 N reaction on screw 2, which is on the E|F fin. That fin is hung above the board (bottom z21.5 from y176 to 195.8), so its only way into the frame is a 13.2 mm base plus the rear-wall joint; the model does not check this. The Ø12 washer centred at y184 spans y178–190, but the boss head starts at y180, so the washer sticks out 2 mm and the nut-trap internals are undefined. At realistic strike speeds, a 3–6-key chord gives screw tensions of 1146–1283 N (felt as designed, 2.3/2.5 m/s) and 1592–1783 N (low-rebound pad), so head-to-fin tension reaches 36–56 MPa: a break. Lever-rod fin holes (Ø3 through 1.6 mm) take 30 MPa bearing at the designer's chord (not reported) and 39–63 MPa at realistic speeds, which will oval the holes into rattling play.
errors.fix: Route the rail load into steel or into a wide PETG section. For example, a steel angle rail whose vertical leg is bolted to the full-width rear wall, or steel standoffs down to the floor plate. Or at least make each boss a solid post onto a full-height fin that is thickened and gusseted under the head, and put no screw on the hung E|F fin. Model the nut-trap internals and the E|F fin as a plate. Add Ø3/Ø6 × 5 bushings or bosses at the lever-rod holes in the fins. Re-check with the speed-defined fff loads.
errors.evidence: loads.py: D–G reactions [58.6, 228.7, 66.6, −12.7] N, matching the designer; screw tension 612 N; 612/(1.6 × 20) = 19.1 MPa. loads2.py: fin reaction 145 N → 30 MPa bearing; 303 N → 63 MPa at 2.3 m/s. geometry: fender_washer 12, screw_y 184, boss_y 180–200.

errors.issue: The claim that 'after 90°/flip the key re-seats by itself' holds only because the model gives the notch lips no friction (Dyn applies only a normal force at the lips). The lip contact is 15.3° from vertical against a friction angle of 14°. One press re-seats the key.

errors.issue: The up-stop timing numbers (must-fix 10) leave out the notch seating: 0.05 mm cloth clearance plus cloth set, about 0.08–0.13 mm at the rod, amplified about 3.75× at the cap. The 0.69 mm black-shim procedure and the stated 'cap just touches' geometry are therefore off by 0.3–0.5 mm.

errors.issue: Two things are only located by friction. (1) Nothing locates the key tail in x: the open notch slides freely along the smooth rod, and only the front guide (y10.5–27) locates the key. (2) The lever hub is printed at Ø3.1 on an h6 Ø3 rod over an 11 mm hub, which allows ±0.52° of yaw: ±0.48 mm at the lever front. Two neighbours yawing toward each other, plus the 0.3 axial play, use up 1.26 of the 1.3 mm lever-lever gap. The clearance sweep includes neither kind of play.

vs.lens: GEOMETRY/BUILD, round 1 adversarial check of W1+. I rebuilt the clearance check from geometry.json with my own polygon code. I took the extreme poses from the designer's own 4-DOF Dyn model. I also checked the boss, screw and fin hold-down, the removal and assembly steps, the dims table, masses, bed fit, the spare bay and the end parts.

errors.issue: The up-stop rail hold-down (must-fix 1) cannot be built or loaded as drawn. (a) The M3×10 thumb screw sticks out 2.8 mm below the thin nut. The stack is rail 3 + roof 1.6 + washer 0.8 + nut 1.8 = 7.2 mm, so the tip ends at z60.75, 2.70 mm below the boss bottom z63.45. At the three interior bosses the screw axis lies in the plane of the 1.6-mm fin (x28.5, 69.76, 123.7), so the tip hits the fin top and the head stays 2.7 mm above the rail: the rail is never clamped. At the right-end boss (x159.3) the tip is not over a fin but over lever B: clearance is 0.08 at a normal dip and −0.20 (collision) at ff. (b) The D12 fender washer at y184 spans y178–190, but the boss starts at y180, so the washer sticks 2.0 mm out of the nut trap. (c) Each boss head is joined to its fin only through a 1.6×20 section (and the nut cavity leaves a 0.1 floor). The prying couple (screw 2.68R at y184 up, 1.68R at y200 down) bends that joint. The designer reports 'fin tension 12.9 MPa', but the joint stress is 77.5 MPa under the designer's own 6-key chord. For single notes it is 31 MPa (fff on C, because the rail overhangs from the first screw) and 42.5 MPa (fff on B, where the right-end boss sits 4.2 mm off its fin and bends it about the weak axis). Even an mf hit on B gives 15.4 MPa. All of this is tension across printed layers (PETG 51 MPa bulk), repeated on every note.
errors.evidence: boss_check.py: stack 7.20, tip z60.75; 'fin under the shank [[27.7,29.3]]' etc.; lever B side wall R vs shank 0.08 (dip) / −0.20 (ff) (misc_check.py). Washer D12 front wall −2.0. Rail FE reproduces the designer's 228.3 N (designer 229.2) and prying 2.68. Joint stresses: chord 77.5 MPa at x69.8; single fff C 31.3, B 42.5 (17.3 in-plane + 25.1 weak axis). DESIGN.md §6 reports only 'fin tension 12.9 MPa'.
errors.fix: Rebuild the hold-down load path. (1) Extend every boss head back to the rear wall (y180→209) and fuse it into a full-width printed bridge beam at y200–209, z58–67.75. Above z56.7 nothing moves behind y200: the lever's highest point there is z56.6 at ff and at the 16.8° service swing. The joint is then the bridge/rear wall, not a 1.6×20 fin top. (2) Move the screws to y≥188 so the D12 washer sits inside the boss with ≥2 mm walls; the prying factor becomes (200−157.1)/12 = 3.6, so recompute. (3) Use M3×8 (or a screw length equal to the stack) with a ≥1.0 solid floor, and cut a Ø3.4 relief in the fin/bridge under each tip. Keep the right-end tip out of lever B's envelope (≥1.3 at ff). (4) Put the 4th screw on a fin plane or on the bridge, not 4.2 mm off the end fin. Re-run the chord case and single fff on C and B, and require <5 MPa cyclic at every printed joint.

errors.issue: Nothing locates the keys sideways at the rear, so the keys can yaw freely. The key sits in an open notch on a continuous Ø4 rod, in a continuous groove, with no saddles or pin. The tail beam passes under the carrier lips with 3.5 mm z clearance. Only the front guide tab (with bushing cloth) fixes x. The tail can swing until its walls touch the neighbour: 0.59° for white keys (1.3 gap at y146, guide at y20.3) and 1.30° for black (1.354 gap, guide at y86.3). The capstan then moves 1.7 mm (white) or 2.1 mm (black) sideways. At rest only friction holds the yaw: 96 N·mm white, 35 N·mm black. When a module is carried on its end (R18), gravity no longer loads the rod or the capstan, the tails swing, and friction keeps them there once the module is laid flat. So the swept 1.30-mm tail gaps (1.00 after tolerance) are not held by anything. Keys will rub their neighbours. Must-fix 9's saddles, which would have given x-location, were dropped.
errors.evidence: misc_check.py yaw limits 0.59° / 1.30°, capstan shift 1.74 / 2.14 mm. model_v4.key_prisms and fixed_prisms have no rear or balance x-feature. The balance rail polygon is the same over x0.3–164.2, and the key rod runs the full width.
errors.fix: Add a balance-pin equivalent. Stand a Ø2 steel pin (or a 2×2 printed rib) on the balance rail at y≈136.5, rising to z≈27, and engage it in a 2.2-wide felt-lined slot in the balance block that opens toward −y. The key then pivots about a located point, like a piano balance pin. The 3-mm forward removal slide still works because the pin leaves the front-open slot after about 1.5 mm. Then re-run the key-key tail clearances with a ±0.1 yaw allowance.

errors.issue: The levers were swept at b=0, which is not their real rest pose. The designer's own settled rest is b=−1.10° (white) and −0.57° (black), because of the capstan felt set. On every release the lever swings further down: −2.63° (white) and −1.43° (black), taken from their Dyn model. In those poses the lever front comes forward toward the dust-cover curtain and down toward its own key's beam. geometry.json side_rest is also b=0, so drawings will show every lever 1.1° too high.
errors.evidence: sweep_indep.py: lever C/D/E/F/G/A/B vs cover curtain: 1.30 at b=0 → 0.95 at settled rest (0.65 after tolerance) → 0.48 at return overshoot (0.18 after tolerance). G# 1.12/0.85, A# 1.30/1.08. sweep2.py: carrier front-bottom vs own key beam at overshoot 1.04 (0.74 after tolerance). dyn_extremes.json: rest_b −1.100/−0.568, b_min_after_release −2.635/−1.434.
errors.fix: Add 'settled rest' and 'return overshoot' lever poses, taken from Dyn, to the sweep and to geometry.json. Move the curtain forward 0.9 mm to y145.3–146.5. That gives lever vs curtain 1.33 at overshoot; the white key rear lip still clears the curtain bottom z45.2 by 1.33 at dip. Chamfer the carrier front-bottom corner 1.5×1.5 (y148.7–150.2, z32–33.5) to get ≥1.3 over the own beam.

errors.issue: The right-end thumb screw head overlaps the next module's cover. Its DIN 653 head is Ø12 at x159.3, so it spans x153.3–165.3. The module edge is x164.5 and the next module's cover starts at x164.7, so the head overlaps it by 0.6 mm; the same happens against the C8 end part. The own cover hole (Ø13.6, x152.5–166.1) also runs 1.8 mm past the cover's own edge at x164.3, yet cover_mass subtracts it as a full hole. Neighbouring covers cannot lie flat.
errors.evidence: misc_check.py: 'head at x159.30 spans 153.30–165.30 … neighbour cover starts x164.7 → overlap 0.60'.
errors.fix: Move the 4th screw to x≤156.5, so the head edge is at 162.5 and the hole edge at 163.3, leaving ≥1.0 of cover web. Or fold it into the rear-wall bridge proposed in finding 1. Add fixed-to-fixed checks across the module seams (covers, rails, heads).

errors.issue: The end parts were never swept, and the end keys sit 0.65 mm from the cheeks (0.35 after tolerance). Narrowing the white heads to 22.2 left A0's left side at x0.65 against the left cheek face x0, and C8's right side at x22.85 against the cheek face x23.5. v3 had 0.5 there, but its comb key was laterally stiff; W1+ keys are only guided at the front (see finding 2). geometry.json has no end-part prisms and no end-part boss or screw positions ('2 thumb screws each' is text only).
errors.evidence: misc_check.py: A0 and C8 cheek gap 0.65 (after tolerance 0.35). run_all.py and clearance_sweep include only module keys and seam neighbours. end_parts() returns levers and fins but no boss_x or screw_x.
errors.fix: Narrow the A0 head to x1.30–22.85 and the C8 head to x0.65–22.20, or move the cheek faces out by 0.65. Export end-part prisms (cheeks, fins, bosses, screws, rail, cover) to geometry.json and run the same sweep on them.

errors.issue: The tool-free removal procedure (must-fix 13) stops before the key is actually out. Once the tail slides forward past the felt strip (y176.5), the lever falls with nothing to catch it. It drops 30° to the floor (C, C#, D, A, A#, B) or 12.75° onto the control-board components at z20 (D#, E, F, F#, G). That is an 80 g steel lever landing on the RP2040 board, and it has to be lifted by hand to put the key back. §9 step 6 says 'lever untouched … it sits back on the capstan', which contradicts this. A black key also has to rise about 20 mm at its front (about 8° about the tail pad) to clear the white heads (y≤50) before it can come forward; §9 only says 'lift the front out of the guide tab'.
errors.evidence: lever_drop.py: first contact after the key leaves: floor at 30.0° (front-bottom corner at z4.9) or 'board components (<=z20)' at 12.75°; G# lands on key G's skin at 7.25°.
errors.fix: Add a service step and part. Before sliding the tail out, hold the lever up by its R3 cap through the empty slot (the rail is already off), or rest it on a printed 12-mm service block stored in the spare bay (put the block on the board for D#–G). For re-insertion: lift the lever, slide the tail under it, seat the notch, then lower the lever. Write out the black-key lift (front above z45, about 8° about the tail pad) and check that path; my check found the black rear corner clears the lever cap by ≥2.5 on the way up.

errors.issue: The lever-lever and lever-fin clearance of 1.30 ignores the play the designer built in. The spacer rings leave 0.3 axial play per fin segment and are only 1.20–1.24 long, so a hub gap can close to the ring length, 1.20 (0.90 after tolerance). The hub bore is only specified as 'Ø3.1 teardrop → reamer'. At Ø3.1 on a Ø3 h6 shaft, the 11-mm hub lets the carrier front, 54.5 mm away, yaw by ±0.5 mm.
errors.evidence: results.txt A: rings 1.20, 1.20, 1.20, 1.23 … for 1.30 gaps. misc_check.py: min ring 1.20 → 0.90 after tolerance; yaw 0.0091 rad → ±0.50 mm at the carrier front.
errors.fix: Make every ring ≥1.30 long so no gap can close below 1.30, and give the 0.3 play only as extra gap. Find the room by narrowing the carriers to 10.6 (0.8 walls): with gaps of 1.6 the layout needs 12×10.6 + 5×1.6 + 16×1.6 = 160.8 ≤ 164.1. Ream the hubs to Ø3.0 H7 (clearance ≤0.02, yaw ≤0.1 mm). Include ±axial play and yaw in the sweep.

errors.issue: The keeper hook and keeper felt (gc±4.15) sit 0.15 mm inside the guide ribs (white) and the black lower walls (±4.3). Every keystroke slides the ribs past bare PETG across that 0.15 gap, and with ±0.3 FDM it becomes an interference. The designer's EXCLUDE list removed this pair from the sweep as a 'sliding fit'.
errors.evidence: full_sweep.py: 144 records at 0.150 mm (x), e.g. key C at dip, guide rib L vs keeper hook C / keeper felt C.
errors.fix: Narrow the hook and its felt to 7.0 wide (±3.5), which is ≥0.8 inside the ribs and still overlaps the 8.6-wide crossbar. Keep the tab and its cloth as the only guide surface.

errors.issue: Axial retention of both rods is only claimed, not drawn. The groove's 'closed ends' do not exist in geometry.json (the balance rail keeps its groove over x0.3–164.2); if added they would be 0.25-mm walls (rail x0.3 vs rod x0.55), too thin to print. vs.lens: Physics/dynamics, round 2. I rebuilt everything in my own code and did not import model_v4.py: statics by virtual work, a 4-DOF free-notch simulator, Flores contact calibration, loads with the rail as a beam plus torsion, the washer as an axisymmetric plate on an elastic PETG layer, and disc-spring curves. My simulator reproduces every nominal number the designer published to within 1 %. The errors below come from inputs and failure modes the designer's pass criteria leave out, plus three structural calculations I believe are wrong.

errors.issue: Ghost re-trigger happens with nominal parameters once the held finger is light. The designer checked only 1 N and 2 N holds. A relaxed hold of 0.6-0.8 N (20-60 % above DW) is normal for skilled players. After a fff note the lever bounces off its pad (e 0.10) and lifts the key past the 40 % re-arm line. The rise is roughly e_pad^2 x KE_lever / (F_hold - BW_bottom + friction), with KE_lever about 150 N*mm at 2.0 m/s, so the margin depends entirely on e_pad and the hold force.
errors.fix: (1) Add 0.6 N and 0.7 N holds to the ghost criterion. (2) Specify the pad as e <= 0.05 and make that the stage-0 pass line, measured with the real R3 cap at 2.5 m/s. At e 0.05 the worst case is 24 % white and 27 % black; at e 0.07 it is still 42 % and 47 % at 2.5 m/s. (3) Firmware: re-arm at 50 % instead of 40 %. Repetition is still 14.7/15.2 Hz nominal and 13.9/14.1 Hz with doubled friction. Also reject a re-press that comes within about 120 ms of a note-on of 1.5 m/s or more when the peak rise was under 60 % and the descent was under 0.3 m/s. That is the ghost signature: the key falls under about 0.3 N net force at about 0.2 m/s.
errors.evidence: verify2/physics_r2/ghost_hold.txt (constant-force hold, magnet % of travel). White 2.0 m/s: hold 0.55 N gives 70 %, 0.6 N gives 52 % (key front rises 5.9 mm), 0.7 N gives 35 %. White 2.5 m/s: 0.7 N gives 55 %, 0.8 N gives 39 %. Black 2.0 m/s: 0.6 N gives 55 %, 0.7 N gives 37 %. Black 2.5 m/s: 0.7 N gives 63 %, 0.8 N gives 46 %. A finger modelled as a 5-20 g mass on a 1.5 N/mm fingertip does not help: at F0 1.0 N it gives 28-42 %. ghost_pad.txt covers pad e 0.05/0.07/0.10. rep_thr.txt covers t50 and t60. The dt 1 us and 2 us results are identical (dtcheck). Pad friction up to mu 0.5 changes nothing (padfric.txt).

errors.issue: The black-key notch-lift target (<= 0.2 mm) and the 'keeper never touched' claim only hold for the assumed pad stiffness (K 20/30 N/mm^1.5) and a front-felt restitution of 0.20. A modulus estimate for 1T felt on 2-3T low-rebound PU under an R3 x 7.6 cap gives K of about 4-14 (white) and 6-19 (black). With those values, or with felt e at the brief's 0.35, the black key hops off the rod after 2.0 m/s notes and hits the keeper at 2.5 m/s. The mechanism: the black lever stops on its pad first (gap -0.70). The key then rebounds from the front felt as a free body, with the capstan force at 0 and the rod force at 0. Retuning the pad gap does not help, since -0.70 is already the best value. Adding or moving lead to shift the centre of percussion to y62-64 barely helps either.
errors.fix: Hold the notch on the rod mechanically so the target no longer depends on material numbers. Two options: (a) a cloth-lined notch that wraps more than 180 deg and snaps over the Ø4 rod, with lip clearance at rest so there is no constant stress, needing 3-8 N to pull off and released with the removal hook; or (b) a rear hold-down felt 0.3 mm above the balance block. Also write stage-0 pass lines as numbers measured on the real geometry: black pad K >= 25 N/mm^1.5 and front-felt stack e <= 0.22. Until then, report the lift for the whole range of materials, not just the nominal values.
errors.evidence: sens.txt, softpad.txt, padK.txt, blackgap.txt, blackfix.txt, blacklift_hist.txt. Black at 2.0 m/s, lift let go / held 1 N (mm): nominal 0.15/0.11; pad K x0.5 0.46/0.35; pad K 10.6 (PU E 1 MPa) 0.63/0.44; pad K 10.6 at 2.5 m/s 1.15/0.64 with keeper -0.31 (contact); pad K 18.6 0.35/0.28; front e 0.28 0.43/0.22; front e 0.35 0.97/0.36 with keeper -0.17; pad gap -0.20 0.51/0.38. The lift is a free flight 5-14 ms after the bottom (Nc 0, rod 0). System restitution at the bottom is 0.13-0.14 nominal, against the brief's felt e of about 0.35.

errors.issue: The nut-trap roof is not at 1.50 MPa constant stress. The designer spread 459 N evenly over the whole Ø20 washer. In fact the M5 fender washer is only 1.2 mm thick, and the M3 thin nut bears only on the rim of its Ø5.3 hole: the nut is 5.5 mm across flats, so it overlaps the hole by just 0.1 mm. The washer bends, lifts off beyond r of about 6 mm, and puts 80 % of the load inside r 4.8 mm. The peak constant pressure on the 2.6 mm PETG roof is 9.6-14 MPa, 6-9 times the claim and far over the < 2 MPa at-rest target. On the rail side, a point load through 3 mm steel on the same layer still peaks at about 3 MPa.
errors.fix: Remove the washer and nut. Use one tapped SS400 strip, 20 x 4 mm, running along x under the roof through all 9 screws; its line pressure is about 1.5 MPa. Alternatively, use a tapped steel disc Ø20 x 6 (1.95 MPa), or halve the preload and accept lower joint-opening forces. Recompute rest_stresses with a plate-on-foundation model rather than P/area.
errors.evidence: loads.txt, washer section. Axisymmetric Hermite plate FE on a compression-only elastic PETG layer: k 750 / 1350 / 2000 N/mm^3 gives peak 9.55 / 12.1 / 14.0 MPa, contact out to r 6.8 / 6.1 / 5.7 mm, and washer bending 125-173 MPa. A steel disc of t 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 mm gives a peak of 3.8 / 2.7 / 2.2 / 1.95 MPa.

errors.issue: The thumb-screw preload is not robust. Three discs (6 x 3.2 x 0.3, h0 0.15) stacked in parallel reach 459 N at flat, but only across 0.15 mm of travel. The clamp includes the 2.6 mm PETG roof at about 10 MPa peak and two printed faces: the rail on the printed top, and the washer on the bridged or supported pocket ceiling. Plausible bedding-in of 20-80 um plus 7-18 um/yr of creep brings the preload down to about 250-380 N. The designer assumed 8 % relaxation (422 N), which corresponds to only 12 um. As the preload drops, the joint opens on single notes and on ordinary triads. End-part rail loads were never reported: C8 carries its whole load on one screw, and the A0-A#0-B0 cluster opens the joint even at full preload.
errors.fix: Give the stack travel. Either stack the discs 3 in parallel x 3 in series (0.45 mm at 459 N), or use a spring with 1 mm or more of travel. Make the clamp metal-to-metal (the tapped steel strip above). Add a 'retighten until flat after 24 h and after transport' step. Give C8 two screws and the left end part a third. Report end-part loads in results.txt. A secondary point: with an elastic interface, the rail begins lifting at the bridge front edge (y176) at about 0.31 x preload per screw's share of the rail, earlier than the 0.46 x preload full-open criterion.
errors.evidence: loads.txt. Preload after a stack thickness loss of 12 / 30 / 50 / 75 / 100 um: 427 / 378 / 323 / 251 / 174 N. My own beam-plus-torsion rail model, which reproduces the designer's 265 N (single C) and 553 N (F-A# cluster), gives: C-E-G at 2.0 m/s 268 N; C-E-G at 2.5 m/s 339 N; cluster at 1.2 m/s 339 N. At a 323 N preload, C and B open at 2.5 m/s (opening force 185 N against a 193 N peak). At 236 N, C, B, E and G open at 2.0 m/s (135-149 N against 152 N). End parts: C8 332 N at 2.0 m/s and 421 N at 2.5 m/s (the preload is 422); A0+A#0+B0 at 2.0 m/s 559 N (opens).

errors.issue: The stress at the bridge-fin junction (tension across layers) is computed as uniform, 'screw share / (t_fin x 33)'. But the screw pulls at y186, 6.5 mm in front of the centroid of the fin section (y176-209). The section therefore also carries a bending moment, and tension peaks at the fin's front edge. For key C at 2.0 m/s, the end fin (1.6 mm) takes 219 N and peaks at about 9 MPa (roughly 6-7 MPa if the rear-wall seam takes about 30 %). The designer reports 4.58 MPa, and their own cyclic limit is 5 MPa. In the 6-key chord at 2.0 m/s, fin 4 takes 965 N and reaches about 35 MPa. That is above PETG's strength across layers (about 25-30 MPa), so the fin could crack, not just sit 'near the rare-case limit'.
errors.fix: Include the eccentricity: sigma = N/A + N e / Z. Then either (a) move the load path to the tapped steel strip spanning the fins and the rear wall, which spreads each pull along x, or (b) thicken the fins to 3 mm, with a fillet of R5 or more at the front of the bridge and fin roots. Screws at y192 remove e but raise the prying factor to 2.9. Also sum the chord peaks with a realistic spread in timing (5-20 ms) and not all at the same instant.
errors.evidence: Hand check using the designer's own screw tensions and lever-rule fin shares (metrics.json stress.holddown: single C 265 N, share 0.83; chord fin loads [3.7, 100, 769, 965, 284] N). End fin: A = 1.6 x 33 = 52.8 mm2, Z = 290 mm3, so 219/52.8 + 219 x 6.5/290 = 4.15 + 4.90 = 9.05 MPa. Fin 4: 965/59.4 + 965 x 6.5/326.7 = 16.2 + 19.2 = 35.4 MPa.

errors.issue: The up-stop cap puts an R3 outer rounding over a square steel corner. The arc centre (lever frame) is at (152.2, 52.5); the steel front-top corner is at (150.0, 54.5), 2.973 mm away. That leaves about 0.03 mm of PETG over the corner, which cannot be printed. At the dip the pad contact centre is only about 1.6 mm from that corner, well inside the contact patch (half-width about 2.7 mm). So every fff note (150-220 N) drives the saw-cut steel edge into the felt/PU pad through a sliver or a slot, cutting the pad and making the noise the blog warned about. The brief required 'steel front-top corner rounded R >= 2 + printed/felt cap'.
errors.fix: Radius or chamfer the steel's top-front edge to R2 or 1.5 x 45 deg (a file jig for 88 blocks). That gives about 0.8 mm of PETG over the corner. Alternatively, use cap R1.5 with a 1.5 mm cap. Add a minimum-wall check between the outer cap profile and the steel box to the model.
errors.evidence: model_v4.py lever_prisms/bump_crown: cap_c = (y_lever_front + 3, z_st + lip - 3) = (152.2, 52.5); steel box sf = 150, z_st = 54.5; |(152.2, 52.5) - (150, 54.5)| = 2.973 < R 3.0. geometry.json key_points, rest pose: cap centre (151.84, 51.51) against steel corner (149.61, 53.47), also 2.97 apart.

errors.issue: Key roll from the beam offset (up to 1.67 mm on F and B) has no capacity check. The metrics' 'roll' field is just 6 N x offset. Restoring over overturning moment, taken as (rod reaction x half block width) / ((capstan - rest pad) x offset), is 4.6 or more at rest. It drops to 1.28 for F and B, and 1.91 for G#, during a held 2.0 m/s stroke. It is 0 during the let-go flight, because the rod is unloaded, so roll is then held only by the guide tab and balance pin.
errors.fix: State the x fit of the guide tab (felt, ±0.05 mm) as the roll restraint and check it. Alternatively, cut the F and B lever offsets by using shorter rings at E|F and B|C.
errors.evidence: roll.txt

errors.issue: The DW band is missed at some points: 46.2 g at the white lip (y0) against 47-55 g; black 55.8 g with doubled friction; black UW 17.4 g near the bottom with doubled friction, against 20 g or more. The geometry.json key prisms omit the ribs, magnet-boss tube and block web that the mass model contains, so drawings made from them give keys about 2.2 g lighter: 20.85 g from voxelised prisms plus bought parts, against the 23.10 g mass model. That shifts DW by about +1 g.
errors.fix: Aim for 52 g at y13, which gives 47.1 g at y0. Export the ribs, boss tube and web into geometry.json so the mass model and the drawings match.

confirmed: Statics reproduced independently by virtual work with exact kinematics. White DW/UW/BW 50.95/42.98/46.97 g; friction 3.98 g (key rod 0.87 + lever rod 0.68 + capstan 0.51 + guide 1.93). Black 51.03/41.44 g, friction 4.80 g. j0 3.229 / 1.863. Stroke curve, doubled-friction curve, y0 46.2 g, y90 128.6 g and front/back ratio 2.52 all match.
m_eff 66.7 / 64.6 g (key 8.8 + lever 57.9). Lever inertia is plausible (steel alone 87,339 g*mm^2 about L). Key I_K from voxelised prisms is within 4 % (white) and 9 % (black).
Flores input calibrations reproduced exactly: e_eff 0.35/0.30/0.20/0.10 gives inputs 0.388/0.3414/0.2454/0.138. The effective e does not depend on mass or speed for this law.

My independent 4-DOF simulator reproduces the designer's dynamics: settled front 43.500 / 55.440; lever -1.104 / -0.594 deg; bottom speeds; up-stop peaks 151/172 N (2.0 m/s) and 192/218 N (2.5 m/s); notch lifts 0.094/0.147 (let go) and 0.115 (black, hold 1 N); ghost 16/18 % (1 N, 2.0 m/s) and 23/30 % (1 N, 2.5 m/s); 2 N-hold rise 1.03/1.10 mm; keeper minimum 0.08 (white, 2.5 m/s staccato).

Repetition holds up. t40 29.6/28.7 ms and full return 51.2/49.1 ms are reproduced. With no felt re-expansion t40 is 31.5/30.7 ms, and with that plus doubled friction 33.0/32.8 ms, i.e. 15.2/15.3 Hz, still above 13.3 Hz. A 1-DOF rigid model agrees with the 4-DOF once friction uses the dynamic contact forces (34.1 vs 34.8 ms frictionless). A 1-DOF model that uses static-equilibrium friction overstates the delay (38.3 ms).

The lever-rod peak reaction is mostly horizontal (95 N in y against 13 N in z at 2.0 m/s), because the pad sits beyond the lever's centre of percussion (39.5 mm vs 44.9 mm). The designer's magnitude, 95/106 N, is right.

Rail model: my beam-plus-torsion code gives the same screw tensions (single C 265 N, F-A# cluster 553 N). The disc spring is 153 N at flat per disc (Almen-Laszlo, h0 0.15), so 3 in parallel gives 459 N.

Friction at the up-stop pad (mu 0.3-0.5), which the model omits, lowers the up-stop peak (151 to 127 N) and the lever-rod reaction (95 to 66 N) and does not change ghosting, so leaving it out is conservative. Balance-pin friction is zero for centred loads.

Constant stresses in the keys and levers (thin tail 0.42/0.46 MPa, beam 0.16, hub 0.02, notch cloth 0.02) are below 2 MPa. Sensor over-travel (black 2.5 m/s pad penetration 1.40 mm, same as the designer's) agrees.

vs.lens: GEOMETRY/BUILD, round 2 (W1+ r2). I wrote my own polygon/prism distance code (glib.py) and swept geometry.json in every exported pose plus q-poses, notch-lift poses and a 12° service pose. Neighbour modules sat at ±164.5, with yaw ±0.1 on keys and levers, and I swept the end parts too. I re-ran the designer's 4-DOF strikes with the key's planar state recorded (model imported read-only) to get time-resolved clearances. Separate checks covered the removal procedure, lever swing limits, cover play, the thumb-screw/washer layout, the dimension tables against the polygons, masses, bed fit and the spare bay.

errors.issue: The rail hold-down cannot be built as drawn. D04/S19 put an M5 fender washer Ø20×1.2 under every one of the 9 thumb screws, all at y186 in the same roof layer. P13 spaces the screws only 15.5-22.1 mm apart. Result: 6 of the 8 neighbouring washer pairs inside a module overlap each other. Both end washers stick 2.2 mm out past the bridge ends (x−2.0 and x166.5), into the next module's bridge. Across every seam the two modules' end washers overlap by 4.0 mm (left end part/O1: 4.0; O7/C8: 0.25). So the modules cannot be pushed together, and the claim '와셔는 주머니 안' is false for 8 of the 9 washers. Geometry.json has no washer or pocket prism, and fixed_fixed_checks only tests heads, covers, rails and end fins.
errors.fix: Replace the round Ø20 washers with rectangular steel nut plates about 12 (x) × 30 (y) × 2 mm, cut from 2T×12 flat bar, long axis along y and centred at y186 (y176-206). Pocket stays open at the front. Bearing area ≈351 mm², so 459 N gives 1.31 MPa (still under 2). Web between plates ≥3.5 mm even at the 15.5 spacing, and the end plates stay 2 mm inside the module (x2-14 / x150.5-162.5). Alternative: fewer screws spaced ≥21.5 mm and ≥11 mm from the ends, then redo the rail FE. Either way, export washer/pocket prisms into geometry.json and add washer-washer and cross-seam checks to fixed_fixed_checks.
errors.evidence: washer_check.txt. Screw x: 8.0, 24.5, 41.66, 63.8, 83.32, 104.5, 123.84, 141.0, 156.5 → in-module overlaps 3.50, 2.84, 0.48, 0.66, 2.84, 4.50 mm. Left washer x−2.0..18.0, right x146.5..166.5 against bridge ends x0.2/164.3. Seam: x156.5 and x172.5 are 16.0 apart, so a 4.0 mm overlap. The largest round washer that fits (1.5 web, 1.0 to the ends) is Ø13.6, giving 3.37 MPa constant bearing, which fails the <2 MPa target that depends on Ø20.

errors.issue: Roof bending is left out while the joint is closed. The rail, screw, nut and washer are tied to the frame only through the 2.6 mm roof over each nut pocket. The roof therefore carries the full separating load T at every strike, whether the joint is open or closed: T = washer force − rail contact force on the roof = F_pad + fulcrum reaction = 2.18·F_pad. The model computes roof bending only when T > preload and reports 0.0 MPa for closed cases. At the fin-plane screws (x41.66/83.32/123.84) the pocket also cuts through the fin top over y176-196. The load therefore has to go round the pocket, which fin_share's direct screw→fin path does not account for.
errors.fix: Report the closed-joint roof bending for every case and put it into the stage-0 fatigue test. Make the roof ≥3.5 mm, or use nut plates as in the critical fix (one-way span 12 instead of a 20 mm three-sided plate). Move the three fin-plane screws ≥8 mm off the fin planes so no pocket cuts a fin.
errors.evidence: model_v4.holddown_loads: roof_bending_if_open = 3pa²/(4t²) if T > Pw else 0. Using the designer's own clamped-plate formula with T: single key 2.0 m/s (key C, T 265 N) 9.6 MPa at every fff; 2.5 m/s 12.2 MPa; 6-key 6 N chord 8.9 MPa (reported 0.0); 6-key 2.0 m/s 20.1 MPa (same as reported). The pocket is open at the front, so the real plate stress is higher than this clamped-circle estimate.

errors.issue: The dust cover's positional play is not in the sweep. The cover is located only by Ø13.6 holes over Ø12 screw heads (±0.8 radial). The rear skirt stops forward movement only. So the curtain can sit 0.8 further back and ±0.8 sideways. Lever ↔ curtain drops from the reported 1.73 to 0.93 nominal (0.63 after ±0.3). Black-key rear wall ↔ curtain notch edge drops from 1.70 to 0.90 nominal (0.60 after tol).
errors.fix: Locate the cover properly: two Ø3 pins standing on the bridge through the rail into Ø3.2 cover holes (±0.1), or head holes of Ø12.4. Or move the curtain forward to y≤144.5 and widen the black notch to ±7.8. Then re-sweep with the cover's play included.

errors.issue: The key yaw model has no lateral play at the front guide. The sweep pivots each key about the tab centre with ±0.1 only at the balance pin. By the model's own numbers the tab has play: rib inner faces are 8.6 apart, the tab is 7.5 wide, and 0.5T bushing cloth goes on each side, leaving ±0.05. Cloth compliance under sideways finger force adds more. With ±0.05 at the tab, every white head/tail gap falls to about 1.20 nominal, i.e. 0.90 after ±0.3, below the 1.0 rule.
errors.fix: Add the tab's lateral play (±0.05 geometric, plus a measured cloth compliance, say ±0.1) to yaw_inflate. Either restore the gap (head 22.04 → head gap 1.46, E|F and B|C tail gap 1.62) or make the tab fit line-to-line (tab 7.6 with 0.5T cloth) and verify the compliance in stage 0.

errors.issue: Getting the disc springs 'pressed flat' by hand is not a reliable stop, and the single-key 2.0 m/s pass depends on it. Three nested DIN 2093 6×3.2×0.3 springs have only h0 ≈ 0.15 mm of travel, about 108° of an M3 turn, so the user cannot feel when they go flat. Reaching 459 N needs ≈0.30 N·m (μ 0.15, head on the springs at r≈2.3) on a knurled head only Ø12 × 2.5 tall. That is near the limit of a fingertip pinch, and it has to be done 9 times for every single-key removal. At ~0.15 N·m the preload is ≈230 N, below the 265 N a single key needs at 2.0 m/s (key C), so the joint would open on every fff.
errors.fix: Make the preload independent of finger torque. Options: fewer and larger fasteners (e.g. 5 × M4 with Ø25 printed knobs, rail FE redone); or a printed Ø30 driver key, stored in the bay, that fits over the knurl. Add a stage-0 test: load cell under the rail plus torque reading, to confirm ≥422 N is reached and held.
errors.evidence: T = F·(0.16·P + 0.58·μ·d2 + μ·r_head) = 459·(0.08 + 0.233 + 0.345) ≈ 0.30 N·m. DESIGN D03/§9 step 10 ('손으로 조인다 = 459 N, 공구 없음'); §7 single-key 2.0 m/s demand 265 N; F_open for key C 242 N at the working preload.

vs.lens: PHYSICS/DYNAMICS round 3: independent mass model from geometry.json prisms, rigid 1-DOF statics/return, and an independent 4-DOF free-notch model (dyn4.py) that reproduces the designer's runs (up-stop 185 N, 0.6 N ghost 20 %/42 %, t50 35.0 ms) before testing the as-built geometry.

errors.issue: The up-stop pad faces (S15) come from a snapshot taken while the key was still bouncing. held_bottom() reads the state at 320 ms (200 ms settle + 120 ms ramp + 200 ms), but at that moment the white lever is still turning at 0.58 rad/s after the ramped key hit bottom. The same routine sets z_us_w/z_us_b (model_v4.py 2117-2121), the end-part pads (2939) and the capstan-adjustment table (run_all.py 610-614). With the pads as modelled, the white lever reaches its pad about 0.7 mm before the key reaches its front felt. The design says the white key reaches its felt first (+0.20). Built per §11 (0.20 feeler at 1 N for white, 0.79 shim for black), the instrument no longer matches the simulation. White repetition then misses 13.3 Hz, the white notch lift exceeds 0.2 mm at the pass-line materials, and black capstan and beam loads roughly double.
errors.evidence: My 4-DOF at 320 ms matches the designer's 'settled' state: b 10.82 deg (designer 10.76), cap top 64.74 (64.69), front z33.84 (33.87). At 600 and 1200 ms, when it is truly settled (|w| < 1e-7 rad/ms), white is b 11.88 deg with cap top 65.60 and black is cap top 64.51. Actual gaps: white 64.89 - 65.60 = -0.71 (design +0.20), black -0.47 (design -0.70). The designer's own results.txt shows white 'push 0.8 N: front 0 N, up-stop 16 N'. Static load split with the designer's pads: white held at 0.6/0.8/1.0 N puts 0 N on the front felt, 0.16/0.34/0.51 N on the pad and 1.9/2.5/3.1 N on the capstan. Release from a 1 N hold with the designer's pads gives t50 35.0 ms (designer 35.2). That fast return comes from the capstan felt being pre-compressed to about 2.9 N between the pad and the finger. As adjusted per §11 (capstan screwed in 0.288 mm, lever rest -2.26 deg), white t50 is 37.9 ms (13.2 Hz), 40.2 ms with friction x2 (12.4 Hz); raising the pad instead gives 38.2/40.9 ms (13.1/12.2 Hz). As adjusted with pass-line materials, white 2.5 m/s staccato lift is 0.237 mm and keeper gap -0.08 (contact). Black as adjusted: capstan peak 22.2 N at 2.0 m/s (designer 11.8), which puts 13.2 MPa on the hidden beam (8 x 6.7 section, arm 35.6); the largest beam stress the designer reports is 11.9 MPa.
errors.fix: Take S15 from a real static equilibrium: a static solve, or a settle of at least 600 ms with |w| < 1e-6 rad/ms. That gives white pad face 65.80 (pad stack 0.91 thinner) and black 63.81 (0.23 thicker). Otherwise, restate §11 so it describes the geometry that was simulated. Then make the assist spring standard on white keys: as adjusted it gives 14.2 Hz, 13.4 Hz with friction x2. Re-run the dynamics, ghost grid, lift/keeper cases, loads, end parts and the capstan-adjustment table. Re-sweep clearances for the new lever rest (-2.26 deg) and overshoot angles.

errors.issue: The snap-notch retention criterion ('snap pull < minimum pull-off 4 N') does not match the lip law in the model itself. The model treats the lip corners as rigid points on the ends of the R2.05 arc, with cloth K 120 N/mm^1.5 and mu 0.25. With that law the static pull-off is about 2.0 N, not 4-8 N. The pulls the model reports (2.72 N nominal, 3.8 N with bad materials) are already above this capacity. In the model the key is held by the velocity-dependent Flores damping force, not by the snap.
errors.evidence: snap.py, quasi-static vertical pull: the lips only touch after 0.20 mm of lift. Holding force is 0.55 N at 0.30 mm lift, 1.23 N at 0.40 mm, and peaks at 1.99 N at 0.64 mm (mu 0.35: 2.60 N; mu 0: 0.67 N). The key pops out at 0.80 mm lift. In my runs lipV reaches 2.3-2.9 N, and 4.0-5.9 N with the damping floor set to 0.1 m/s, while lift stays at 0.13-0.21 mm. Stage-0 test 4 asks for 4-8 N, which 0.09 mm of cloth squeeze per side cannot give. Its remedy (0.6T cloth) would make the lined notch R1.95, smaller than the R2.0 rod, if the cloth covers the whole notch, so the key would bind. Upside down in transport, a shock of about 2.0/0.23 = 8.7 g pops a key.
errors.fix: Judge retention by lift against the 0.80 mm pop-out lift and report that margin. Drop the 4 N force comparison, or calibrate the lip law to a stage-0 force-lift curve. If a 4-8 N snap is required, get it from the lip lands alone (a narrower entry of about 3.70 mm with cloth only on the lips, or a steeper lip angle) and check that the lips still clear the rod by at least 0.05 at rest. Correct the stage-0 remedy so it does not change the running notch radius.

errors.issue: The ghost re-trigger grid starts at 0.6 N. A lightly resting finger at 0.45-0.55 N (above the 0.43 N rest UW) lets the key rise 70-99 % after a 2.5 m/s note. That is above the 60 % peak limit of the firmware filter, so the filter cannot drop it, and the key then comes back down slowly and plays a soft ghost note. The filter also drops real soft repeats (< 0.3 m/s) within 120 ms of a loud note.
errors.evidence: Holding 0.5 N after 2.5 m/s: white 84 % (designer pads) and 81 % (as adjusted), black 78 %/74 %. The key comes back down at 0.03-0.12 m/s, with the peak 72-115 ms after the bottom. Holding 0.55 N as adjusted: white 47 % (61 % with the spring, 82 % with the spring and pad e 0.07), black 53-77 %. The cause is the lever dropping back onto the capstan after the pad hit. The pad rebound itself is only e_sys 0.061.
errors.fix: Add 0.45-0.55 N holds to the ghost grid. In firmware, after a note of 1.5 m/s or more, ignore re-presses slower than about 0.12-0.15 m/s for 250 ms, or require the magnet to reach 90 % before re-arming when the rise was slow. Do not use the peak < 60 % rule. On the mechanical side, lower capstan-felt e (0.35 to about 0.2) or reduce the lever's travel above the capstan at the bottom.

errors.issue: The notch-lift and keeper pass/fail results depend on a numerical parameter: the Flores onset-velocity floor V0_FLOOR = 0.02 m/s, which sets the damping of every contact that starts slowly (notch cloth, lips, capstan).
errors.evidence: With v_floor 0.1 m/s: white as modelled at 2.0 m/s, lift goes from 0.105 to 0.155 mm (+48 %). White as adjusted at 2.5 m/s, lift goes from 0.163 to 0.205 mm, over the 0.2 target, and keeper gap drops to 0.05. Black lipV rises from 2.7 to 5.9 N.
errors.fix: Use a contact damping law that does not depend on the onset speed (Hunt-Crossley or Kelvin, with damping measured in stage 0) for the cloth, lip and capstan contacts, or report the lift and keeper results over v_floor 0.02-0.1 and keep margin against 0.2 mm.

errors.issue: Nothing positively limits the thumb-screw preload. Once the 3x3 disc stack is flat (459 N), any extra turn loads the joint solid, and with the 30 mm driver a hobbyist can easily go past 0.3 N m. The constant roof bearing stress then goes well over the 2 MPa limit.
errors.evidence: My finite beam on a Winkler layer gives 1.85 MPa peak at 459 N, 1.92 MPa with the 3.4 mm screw hole (designer 1.90), so the design value holds. At 0.5-0.6 N m (preload about 800-1000 N at K 0.2) the peak is about 3.2-4 MPa constant. The Almen-Laszlo check gives 152.8 N per disc when flat, matching the designer.
errors.fix: Use a slip-clutch (torque-limiting) printed driver set to 0.30 N m, or a steel crush sleeve or shoulder under the head so the screw bottoms out at the flat-stack length.

errors.issue: Doubled friction pushes DW and bottom UW outside the targets. The designer knows this but it is unresolved. Black capstan friction is 2.0 g of the 4.8 g total because the capstan slips 4.8 units per unit of key rotation.

confirmed: Statics are right: my prism mass model with my own virtual-work code gives white DW/UW 52.0/44.0 g at y13, 47.2 at y0 and 131.2 at y90, a ratio of 2.52. Black at front+10 is 50.5/40.9 (51.4/41.8 with the designer's mass). All within 1 %.
Friction breakdown is reproduced: white key rod 0.88, lever rod 0.72, capstan 0.46, guide 1.93 g; black 1.14/0.22/1.97/1.48 g.

Mass and inertia: key D 23.62 g (designer 23.29), lever 79.50 g with I_L 90452 (designer 90630). m_eff is 68.9 white and 65.5 black (designer 64.7). Black I_K is 9 % higher in my prism model; this changes DW by less than 1 g.

My independent 4-DOF model reproduces the designer's dynamics at the modelled pad heights: white 2.0 m/s gives 185 N up-stop, 69 N front felt, lift 0.105 (designer 0.096); 0.6 N hold 20 % (19 %); black 2.5 m/s 0.6 N 42 % (42 %); t50 35.0 ms (35.2). Halving the time step from 3 to 1.5 us does not change these results.

Restitution: each contact law gives its design e in a single-body drop test (10 g at 0.1 m/s and 60 g at 2 m/s). In the full system the lever-on-pad e is 0.061 (design 0.06) and the key-on-front-felt e is 0.10-0.14.

The faster return in the 4-DOF model compared with the rigid 1-DOF (43 ms) is physical: with friction removed the two give 36.4 and 38.3 ms. The 1-DOF uses static reactions for friction, while the dynamic capstan force during the return is only about 0.5 N.

Rest stresses: thin tail 0.41/0.46 MPa and beam 0.16 MPa agree with hand checks. Roof bearing under the tapped strip is 1.85-1.92 MPa at 459 N. Disc-spring flat force is 153 N per disc, so 459 N for 3 in parallel.

Up-stop peaks per key match the designer (white 183-185 N at 2.0 m/s; black 260-265 N at 2.5 m/s), as do lever rod reactions (113-156 N). Single-key joint closure (360 N against 422 N preload) holds using the designer's influence factor; I did not re-derive the rail FE.

Lever roll: the capstan, pad holder and steel are centred on the lever, so there is no lever roll moment. Key roll from the capstan offset is carried by the rod or lip couple and by the front felt at the bottom.
Full return stays under 60 ms in every variant: 54.4 ms white as adjusted, 57.6 ms with friction x2.
Dust-cover/transport tilt: the key's weight (0.23 N) is far below the lip capacity (about 2 N), so keys stay on the rod when tilted, apart from the shock limit noted in the snap finding.

vs.lens: GEOMETRY/BUILD, round 3. I re-checked geometry.json and model_v4.py independently. My own numpy prism sweep covered module, adjacent modules and end parts: keys at rest, 25/50/75 %, dip, ff and over, plus ff/over with the maximum notch lift; levers at rest, b0, 25/50/75 %, dip, ff, dip_rigid and over. Lateral play: tab play plus pin play for keys; yaw plus directional axial float from the ring/boss layout for levers; cover play ±0.10. Pass rule 1.3 nominal, i.e. 1.0 after ±0.3. I also checked cross-seam fixed-to-fixed parts, re-ran the designer's removal_path for all 12 keys (the designer reported 7), the lever swing with the rail off, capstan access, the spring seat, the balance pin against the stepped block, the dims tables against the polygons, masses, print plan and the spare bay, and tested every judge must-fix and graft against the geometry.

errors.issue: The end-part seams are not buildable as exported. (a) end_fixed_prisms() gives the outer seam fins two-sided bosses, as if they were interior fins. The left end part's boss x43.85–48.15 runs past its own edge (x47) into module 1's end fin (x47.2–48.8) and boss (x47.2–50.15): 0.95 mm x-overlap, with the whole Ø7 boss circle overlapping in y/z at y199.75–206.75, z30–37. The right end part's boss x−1.15–3.15 overlaps module 7's end fin (x−1.8 to −0.2) in the same way. (b) The right end part's seam fin (x0.2–1.8) is a full rectangle, y152–209, z5–72.5. It fills the dovetail groove (x0–4, y198–207, z3–17.3) that module 7's rear male tongue drops into. The module's own end fins are notched to z17.9 over y197.7–207.3 for exactly this reason; the end parts are not. (c) The end parts export no dovetail at all. (d) End-part fins lack the 0.1 inset on the y152–176 front extension, so lever B0 to its fin is 1.255 (0.955 after tolerance). (e) end_part_sweep() never includes the adjacent module, so the reported 'end fin gap 0.40' and 'min 1.31/1.32' miss all of this. Result: an end part cannot be lowered onto module 1 or module 7.
errors.fix: In end_fixed_prisms, use one-sided bosses on seam fins (left part [43.85, 46.8]; right part [0.2, 3.15]), as fixed_prisms already does through boss_len. Notch the seam fins (z≥17.9 over y197.7–207.3) the same way as module fins, apply fin_ext_inset, and export the left part's male root/tongue and the right part's female groove. Then add a seam sweep, both fixed-to-fixed and moving, that includes module 1's C/C#/D and module 7's A/A#/B.

Module 7 fin (−1.8, −0.2) vs RIGHT part boss (−1.15, 3.15): −9.25. Module 7's male tongue in the right part's groove vs the right part's fin (0.2, 1.8): −11.0. errors.issue: The black-key guide geometry contradicts the tab play used in every sweep and in the roll check. Black keys have no guide ribs; their low walls, 1.2 thick, straddle the tab with an inner width of 10.4 − 2×1.2 = 8.0. The black tab is 7.5 wide. P31 and assembly step 2 put 0.5T cloth on the tab sides ('탭 폭 7.5 + 천 0.5T 양쪽 … ±0.05', '탭 앞면 천·옆 천'). With that cloth the stack is 8.5 in an 8.0 gap: 0.25 mm per side of interference, crushing the cloth to half its thickness. That gives several N of normal force, and a friction far above the modelled guide_drag of 0.02 N, which could jam the black keys. Without the cloth the play is ±0.25, not the ±0.05 (tab_play) that the model applies to every key. The designer's own removal output shows the bare gap: 'pull up 0.25 (wall L low vs tab C#)'. The roll-check note ('tab 7.5 + 0.5T cloth in 8.6 ribs') describes the white keys only.
errors.fix: Narrow the black tabs to 6.9 (6.9 + 2×0.5 cloth = 7.9 in the 8.0 gap, ±0.05). The keeper hook, ±2.6 wide, still fits. Then give the black keys their real play in the sweep and the roll check. Because the printed rib and wall gaps are ±0.3 while the target play is ±0.05, also add a stage-0 fit coupon, or choose the cloth thickness per batch.
errors.evidence: sweep3_black025.txt (black tab play 0.25): black-white key 1.059 nominal (0.76 after tolerance) against the designer's 1.33; black low wall vs own keeper hook 1.092; A# thin tail (ff with lift) vs lever B 1.082; black thin tail vs fin 1.193. With play 0.05 (sweep3_base.txt) the same pairs are ≥1.3. Geometry: key C# wall L low x16.015–17.215, tab C# x17.465–24.965.

errors.issue: The optional assist spring (judge must-fix 6 / graft 8, the stated fallback for the 13.7/13.8 Hz doubled-friction repetition margin and for black bottom upweight 17.4 g) cannot be built as drawn. (1) Its seat is a Ø7 plate at y168 under the rail, i.e. y164.5–171.5. The pad holders end at y164.0 and the bridge's top edge begins at y170.0, leaving a 6.0 mm slot, so the plate runs 1.5 mm into the bridge. (2) The carrier-side cup sits on the carrier top at (168, 55.5) at b=0. Because the carrier top is 22 mm above L, the cup moves backward as the lever rises: to y171.05 at spring engagement (55 %) and y173.92 at the white rigid bottom (black 170.56 / 172.93). The spring, modelled as vertical, would lean 14–33° and its axis passes through the bridge front face: at y170 it is at z64.0–69.0, inside the solid z65.2–72.5. (3) P18 gives the seat pocket as Ø4.4×0.6 in a 1.0 plate, while D05 gives Ø4.4×1.5, which a 1.0 plate cannot hold.
errors.fix: Redesign the spring. Either use a small torsion spring on the lever rod, with one leg bearing on the bridge underside and the other on the web; it gives pure torque with no sliding and no fight for space under the rail. Or keep a vertical spring but let its lower end slide on a flat steel dish on the carrier top rather than a cup, and fit a Ø≤5.5 seat recessed between y164.2 and y169.8. Then recompute force direction and travel, and make P18 and D05 agree.
errors.evidence: misc_checks.txt: seat and cup kinematics (rot about L=(203.25,33.5)); the bridge polygon starts at (170.0,72.5)/(170.26,65.2); pads y150–164. solved.spring: y_s 168, D_out 4.0, z_seat 72.1.

errors.issue: None of the key adjustments can be made in place, so the procedure in §11 cannot be carried out (judge must-fix 10 is resolved only on paper). Up-stop timing is set by turning the capstan (an M3 button head with a hex socket). The capstan sits under its own lever's felt strip and steel block, and above that are the tapped strip, the rail and the cover. Even with the rail off and the lever pushed to the bridge stop at 15.25°, the felt is only 3.9 mm above the capstan head, which leaves no hex-key access. §11-1 says to set cap-to-pad contact with a 0.79 shim at 1 N, which needs the rail on and the capstan reachable at the same time. Key height (punchings glued under the rest pad) and front putty also need the key out. So every eighth-turn iteration means: cover off, 8 thumb screws out, rail off, hook pull, key out, adjust, then refit and re-flatten all 8 screws, with another 24 h re-tighten. That is repeated for 88 keys.
errors.fix: Move the in-place adjustments to parts that can be reached. Set up-stop timing with 0.1 mm shims under each pad holder (reachable with the rail lifted, no key removal), and set the capstan once on a printed height gauge before the key goes in. Set key level on a bench jig that reproduces the rod and shelf, before insertion. Otherwise, add Ø2.5 access holes through steel, felt, strip and rail at each capstan; note that the black C# capstan (x21.215, y181.55) is 1.8 mm from the x23/y182 thumb screw, so the screw would have to move.
errors.evidence: misc_checks.txt: with the lever at 15.25° the felt bottom above the white capstan is at z34.90 against the head top at z31.0. The bridge contact angle from my own swing check is 15.1–15.25°, matching the model's service_swing of 15.25°. The strip spans y172–192 across each bay; the rail is solid over y150–210.

errors.issue: The r3 stepped balance block brings a PETG face to 0.19–0.26 mm from the steel balance pin, and neither sweep checks it. The pin occupies y135.5–137.5 up to z23.3. The lip-region front wall of the stepped block stands at y137.76 over z20.75–22.3, 0.26 behind the pin's rear face at rest, 0.21 (white) and 0.19 (black) at ff. The printed slot's rear end at y138 is only 0.50 behind the pin, falling to 0.26 at the black ff pose. Both sweeps skip the pair as a 'designed fit', but only the slot's x fit is designed; y is supposed to be set by the notch lips. With ±0.3 FDM the pin can bear on the lip wall, fighting the snap notch's y location and stopping it from seating.
errors.fix: Move the pin forward by about 1.2 mm, to y135.3 (rear face 136.3, giving 1.46/1.39 to the lip wall). Extend the block front and the slot to y134, and move the rail front to y132.3 so the pin hole keeps its 2.0 front wall. Alternatively, move the slot's rear end and the lip wall at least 1.3 behind the pin.

errors.issue: Dims entry D11 still carries the r2 pad specification, 'pad e ≤ 0.12 (drop test)'. The r3 design uses e 0.06 with a stage-0 pass line of e ≤ 0.07 (§16 test 1, DESIGN §6). By the design's own ghost tables, a pad accepted at e 0.10–0.12 gives a 97–99 % magnet rise that the firmware filter does not catch. The value is off by more than 70 % and would lead a builder to accept pads that fail.

errors.issue: Single-key removal is not tool-free, contrary to graft 3's 'removal stays tool-free' and the removal_geometry docstring ('tool-free … fingernail'). It needs the printed Ø30 driver (flattening the discs takes 0.30 N·m, a 50 N rim force on the Ø12 knurl) to take out and refit 8 screws of about 6.5 turns each, then a re-flatten 24 h later, plus the printed hook. A black key needs both white neighbours out first; the designer's model gives −6.55 mm with only one out. Yet assembly step 8 never says to install black keys before their white neighbours. The 72 disc springs per module are not captive. If an L block is forgotten, the levers of E, F, F#, G and G# drop 13–13.5° onto the board components.
errors.fix: State the tools in §10 and in the model. Add 'install the 5 black keys first' to step 8. Make the disc stacks captive with an O-ring under the head. Add a permanent printed lever catch about 1° below rest so a lever with no key can never reach the board. Consider a quarter-turn cam clamp in place of the 8 screws.

errors.issue: The lever-angle window for removal is narrow and shrinks with adjustment. The pull-up raises the lever to 13.95°, and it meets the bridge at 15.1–15.25° (about 0.9° of window if the bridge underside prints 0.3 low). Each eighth-turn of capstan adds 0.25° at the end of the pull-up, so the half-turn cited in §11-1 adds about 2.0°. Past the window, the lever reaches the bridge before the rear notch lip clears the rod.
errors.fix: Relieve the bridge underside at y170–176 by 1.5 mm, or chamfer the carrier's top-front corner, so the lever can reach at least 17°. Also tell the user to push the lever up to the bridge stop, rather than holding it at 14.5°.

C~B 모듈을 z58(레버 윗면과 브리지 사이)에서 잘라 위에서 본 평면. 건반·레버·핀·뒤 선반은 실선, 업스톱 레일·패드·손나사·위치 핀은 보라 가상선, 밸런스 레일·봉 받침·센서 바·캡스턴·자석·핀은 파란 숨은선, 제어 기판·USB 플러그는 초록 점선. 앞은 피치·헤드 폭·틈, 위는 레버 중심·핀·손나사 x, 왼쪽은 y 좌표. A·B는 도면 4의 가로 단면 자리.

레버 구역 x–z 단면 셋. A-A(y203.25 레버 봉): 허브·C-링(P14 길이)·핀 보스 황동 부싱·핀·뒤 선반·리브·USB 플러그·도브테일, 확대로 핀 둘레 축 놀음. B-B(y157 패드 가운데): 레버 캐리어·강철·패드 층(흑 칸 스페이서 0.85)과 누른 레버(점선). C-C(y182 손나사 줄): 손나사·접시 스프링·레일·지붕·탭 강철 띠 주머니.
백건 D를 기준으로 한 부품도: 측면 단면(앞·뒤 두 토막, 모든 z·y 좌표), 윗판을 투명하게 본 평면 투영(벽·리브·블록·빔 x), y 위치별 가로 단면 6개, 아래 표에 백건 7종의 x 범위. y·z 치수는 모든 백건에서 같다.
흑건 C#를 기준으로 한 부품도: 측면 단면(앞·뒤 두 토막, 모든 z·y 좌표), 윗판을 투명하게 본 평면 투영(벽·리브·블록·빔 x), y 위치별 가로 단면 6개, 아래 표에 흑건 5종의 x 범위. y·z 치수는 모든 흑건에서 같다. 추 칸은 납 5 g(닫힌 위쪽) + 출력 뚜껑(나머지 깊이).
레버(백·흑 공통 1종)를 0°로 놓은 부품도. 위: 캐리어 중심 측면 단면(모든 z·y 좌표, R3 캡·모따기·립·펠트·허브). 가운데: 위·밑에서 본 평면(윗 립 사이 강철 폭, 아래 립·펠트 띠)과 강철 블록 부품(옆·앞·위). 아래: y 위치별 가로 단면 6개와 확대 E·F(위 립 0.8×1, 아래 립 1×1)로 강철이 5면에 갇히는 모양.

모듈 프레임 한 덩어리. 평면(브리지 밑을 위에서 봄: 앞 레일·탭·키퍼 훅·흑 멈춤 레일·밸런스 레일과 봉 받침·핀·보스·선반·리브·도브테일, 브리지·위치 핀·띠 주머니·지붕 손나사 구멍 Ø3.4는 가상선/숨은선), 측면 단면 둘(핀 2, C# 중심), 봉 받침 확대, 가로 단면 셋(봉 줄 y141, 손나사 줄 y182: 지붕 구멍 8개, 레버 봉 줄 y203.25)과 형상 표.
